title: Segmented Spillback & Isolation Contracts for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD to define 'Segmented Spillback'—a controlled mechanism that lets reserved pools safely lend unused headroom to opportunistic workloads—and a complementary 'Isolation Contract' primitive that formalizes per-tenant preemption rules, audit trails, and fallbacks. The feature aims to improve overall utilization of Dedicated capacity while keeping predictable latency for paying tenants and preserving strong isolation guarantees for regulated customers. This doc covers high-level goals, user personas, API/console UX, operational controls, autoscale interactions, policy defaults, telemetry, and acceptance criteria.
goals: Increase utilization of dedicated GPU pools by enabling short-lived, auditable spillback of unused reserved headroom to opportunistic tenants without violating SLOs for owners of reserved capacity
Provide a first-class Isolation Contract that encodes preemption allowances, minimum headroom guarantees, emergency eviction policies, and auditability that can be used by billing/entitlement systems
Expose simple console controls and REST API primitives for product teams to opt into spillback windows and to configure contract tiers (strict, mixed, permissive)
Ensure platform tooling (autoscaler, prewarmer, routing) respects contracts and ramps predictably during scale events to avoid cascading preemptions
success_metrics: Platform-wide dedicated GPU utilization increases by >= 8% within 30 days post-launch while P95 generation latency for reserved-tenants remains within +5% of baseline
Reduction in cold-start rate for opportunistic bursts by >= 20% due to spillback prewarming and predictive scaling
< 0.5 incidents/month where spillback caused a reserved-tenant SLA breach (measured by latency and error budget windows)
Audit logs for preemption/spillback events available for 100% of affected requests with tenant-linked metadata
requirements: Runtime: support for a spillback token that annotates a compute slot as temporarily borrowable and tracks originating reserved pool and time window
Scheduler: soft-eviction hooks that prefer gently throttling opportunistic work before evicting reserved replicas; eviction decisions must be reversible within a configurable grace period
Autoscaler: prewarm workflows must be aware of active spillback windows to avoid over-allocating GPUs that would be immediately reclaimed

Console UX: per-reservation 'isolation contract' modal with three default tiers (Strict, Balanced, Flexible), each exposing editable knobs: preemption_tolerance_pct, grace_seconds, max_borrow_rate, audit_level
API: new endpoints for creating/updating Isolation Contracts and for requesting spillback tokens (POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/:id/spillback-request)

Telemetry: emit events for spillback_grant, spillback_revoke, preemption_attempt, preemption_success, preemption_denied; each event must include reservation_id, tenant_id, reason_code, and latency_impact_estimate
Billing: tags emitted so chargeback can reflect opportunistic usage and any penalty credits for preemption-induced degraded performance
Security/Compliance: all preemption decisions and spillback grants must be recorded in the audit log with sufficient context to satisfy SOC2 evidence requests
non_goals: This PRD does not cover multi-tenant physical isolation (dedicated hardware per tenant); it's focused on soft isolation within shared Dedicated pools
No initial changes to the pricing model; billing integration will use existing usage reports plus a spillback tag for visibility only in the first release
Not addressing model-level quality degradation detection (that remains in Optimize/evals scope)
risks: Incorrect eviction heuristics could cause latency spikes for reserved tenants — mitigated by staged rollout and strict default contracts
Telemetry gaps may make it hard to debug rare cross-tenant interference — require schema-gated events before GA
Customers may misconfigure permissive contracts and experience unexpected preemption; require clear console defaults and warning text
Complexity in autoscaler-scheduler coordination may cause oscillation; mitigate with conservative cooldowns and canary region rollout
acceptance_criteria: Config: Console and API support creating an Isolation Contract with the three default tiers and persistence of custom knobs
Spillback lifecycle: A reserved pool with active spillback window can issue spillback tokens and the scheduler allows opportunistic allocations marked with that token

Preemption semantics: When reserved demand returns, the runtime triggers preemption events annotated in the audit log; opportunistic tasks follow graceful throttling for the configured grace_seconds before being evicted

SLO protection: In a controlled synthetic test (50 reserved replicas with steady baseline load + opportunistic borrowers), reserved tenants' P95 token latency must not regress more than 5% relative to the baseline for the strict contract and not more than 10% for the balanced contract
Auditability: For every spillback_grant there is a corresponding audit event within 5 seconds containing reservation_id, borrower_tenant_id, start_ts, expected_reclaim_ts, and operator_reason
Telemetry: All new event types are populated in the internal telemetry pipeline and can be queried on console dashboards and alerted on (sample queries provided in the runbook)
Autoscaler coordination: Prewarm + autoscale runs for sample workloads show <15% overshoot when spillback windows are active (measured over 10 test runs)
Security review: Security accepts the data retention and encryption model for audit logs and the feature toggles are documented in the control plane
Rollout: Feature flag gating is implemented; can enable for up to 5 internal beta tenants and one customer pilot without global impact
dependencies: Scheduler: soft-eviction hooks and token-aware placement (ENG-23456)
Runtime: preemption telemetry and graceful throttling implementation (ENG-24199)
Console: new Contract UI components and API endpoints (DES-41212, ENG-25333)
Billing: spillback tag pass-through on usage export (ENG-26001)
Security: audit-log schema extension and retention policy approval (SEC-330)
Legal: terms update for opportunistic borrowing in Dedicated contracts
